initial_presentation: A 9-year-1-month-old girl visited the Genetic Endocrinology Clinic with concerns about intellectual development and short stature. Her height was 123 cm (-2 SD), corresponding to a height age of 7 years. She weighed 23 kg (-1.3 SD) with a body mass index of 15.2 (25th-50th percentile). Her father's height was 168 cm and her mother's height was 157 cm, giving her a familial target height of 156 cm (-0.85 SD). She was delivered via caesarean section post-term without asphyxia. At birth, she weighed 4.25 kg and measured 50 cm in length. Severe developmental delays were noted during her toddler years; she began walking independently at three years old and could speak a few simple words by five years old. She exhibited distinct facial features, including a coarse face, sparse hair, narrow forehead, ptosis, deep-set eyes, broad nasal tip, short nose, malformed teeth, and large ears with moderately sized earlobes. She had tapering fingers and bilaterally curved fifth fingers, flat feet, and fourth toes shorter than the fifth. Extensive hyperpigmentation was observed, particularly on the lower limbs. No secondary sexual characteristics were present; breast and pubic hair were at Tanner stage B1 and P1, respectively. Thyroid and liver function tests were normal, but she had a complete deficiency of growth hormone. Her stature was below the 3rd percentile, and her bone age was 7 years and 10 months. Recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) injections were started at 0.036 mg/kg/day, but treatment was stopped after three weeks due to edema in both lower extremities.

A 55-year-old female with a 25-year history of diabetes mellitus and a three-year history of hypertension, both managed with medications, presented with swelling on the lateral side of her right foot for one week. The swelling began gradually in the plantar area of the right foot and increased in size, accompanied by pain during walking. The pain was throbbing in nature and did not radiate. Additional symptoms included redness, warmth, pus discharge, and generalized fever. The patient reported no history of trauma. Her medical history includes a 15-year presence of a foreign body (plastic) in the plantar area of her right foot, for which she did not seek medical attention. During a subsequent pregnancy, she experienced fever and swelling in the same area, leading to hospital admission. She underwent bedside irrigation and debridement, multiple incisions and drainage procedures in the operating room, and a three-month hospital stay. She was later referred to another hospital for a skin graft. On examination, there was swelling in the plantar area of the right foot with a 2x3 cm collection, negative fluctuation, warmth, redness, tenderness, and pitting edema on the dorsum of the foot, but no pus or blood discharge. An unhealed ulcer was noted on the lateral aspect of the sole. Neurovascular examination was normal.

A 32-year-old individual presented for a rheumatologic evaluation due to several months of fatigue, dry eyes, dry mouth, weight loss, hair loss, joint pain, and shortness of breath during physical activity.

A 10-year-old female was referred by a urologist for evaluation of hypertension. Her right kidney, which was smaller in size, was removed four months prior. On the day of admission, her brachial blood pressure was recorded at 190/90 mmHg.

A 55-year-old Chinese female presented with exertional dyspnea persisting for over 10 years. Over the past 2 years, she developed truncal obesity and facial rounding, without acne, hirsutism, or wide purple striae. She had a family history of hypertension and was diagnosed with hypertension 10 years ago, for which she had been taking irbesartan, metoprolol, and nifedipine XR. Additionally, she was diagnosed with hyperlipidemia 5 years ago and was on statins. She reported no history of alcohol or drug abuse, including steroid use. On admission, her physical examination revealed elevated blood pressure (164/104 mmHg) and a normal heart rate (74 beats per minute). Her height was 156 cm, weight 51 kg, and waist circumference 88 cm, resulting in a body mass index (BMI) of 20.96 kg/m2. She exhibited a plethoric moon-shaped face, centripetal obesity, buffalo hump, ecchymosis, and slight edema in both lower limbs. Neurological examination was normal except for slight muscle weakness in the lower extremities.

A 46-year-old female with no notable medical or surgical history experienced lower limb weakness and moderate low back pain for four months. She was referred to the National Institute of Neurology and Neurosurgery Manuel Velasco Suarez for further evaluation. Physical examination revealed reduced strength in the lower limbs, with a score of 2/5 in the right pelvic limb and 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in the left pelvic limb according to Daniel's strength scale. Sensory examination indicated hypoesthesia in the T6 dermatome. Patellar and Achilles reflexes were minimally responsive. The patient also reported overflow incontinence and constipation with difficulty evacuating for the past month.

A 15-year-old male presented with pain and limited movement in the left ring finger's metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint. The patient reported a history of trauma one year prior, where his left hand was stepped on during a football game. The patient has asthma and is on inhaled corticosteroids. He denied any numbness or tingling in the affected finger or hand. Clinical examination showed tenderness upon touch and restricted flexion at the fourth MCP joint of the left ring finger. The other fingers on the same hand had normal movement, and there were no signs of neurovascular issues.

A 34-year-old female presented with skin lesions on both lower limbs, accompanied by intense itching for the past 15 years. The lesions showed no seasonal variation and were absent in the oral cavity. No similar lesions were reported among family members. The patient had no history of diabetes or hypertension. Physical examination revealed lichenoid papules on both shins extending to the knees, which were non-tender and had mild scaling. There was no involvement of nails or mucosal areas.

An 18-year-old female began experiencing twisting postures in her feet and a tip-toe gait at the age of five. These symptoms progressively worsened and extended to her neck, trunk, and limbs. Two years after the onset, she lost the ability to walk and became reliant on a wheelchair. Her perinatal history was normal, and her early development showed no abnormalities. There was no family history of similar symptoms and no known exposure to heavy metals. She had a history of iron-deficiency anemia and menorrhagia, with symptom exacerbation noted before menstruation. Neurological examination identified dysarthria and generalized dystonia affecting the face, neck, trunk, and limbs. She exhibited an open-mouthed dystonic smile and slow, writhing movements of her limbs. Deep tendon reflexes were brisk, and plantar reflexes were absent due to dystonia. Her score on the Unified Dystonia Rating Scale (UDRS; maximum score, 112) was 81. Cognitive and ophthalmic examinations, as well as sensory evaluations, were normal.

A 57-year-old female with a seven-year history of difficulty breathing presented to our department in 2021. Since 2014, she had been experiencing shortness of breath and dizziness following physical activities. In 2018, she developed rashes on her neck and chest. In 2020, she was hospitalized due to difficulty breathing. Pulmonary function tests indicated type I respiratory failure and asthma.
